deep.reconstruction:
This page is a draft of the end of §20 and the start of §21 of Riemann's Inaugural-Dissertation (Göttingen 1851, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'). There is no computation on the page. The content is programmatic and states theorems in words.

(1) End of §20, continued from the previous page. A theory built on the dissertation's foundations would first fix the function by its defining conditions. Only afterwards would it pass to its various analytic expressions. The right column, top, reads in substance 'zu den verschiedenen Ausdrücken, deren die Function fähig ist, übergehen'. The character of a class of functions expressible in a similar way by 'Größenoperationen' (arithmetic operations, differentiation, integration) then shows itself in the boundary and discontinuity conditions attached to them.

(2) Example: the theorem on algebraic functions. Let z range over the whole extended plane A, covered once or several times. In modern terms this is a compact Riemann surface X realised as a finite branched covering pi: X -> P^1. Suppose the function w has no discontinuities except isolated poles of finite order. The order of a pole is measured against the local parameter: 1/(z-z') at a finite point z', and z itself at z = infinity. Then w is an algebraic function of z.

In modern form: a meromorphic function on a compact Riemann surface that is an n-sheeted cover of the sphere satisfies P(z,w) = 0 for a polynomial P.

The proof is not given here; the following is my standard completion. Let w_1(z), ..., w_n(z) be the values of w on the n sheets over z. Their elementary symmetric functions are single-valued on the sphere. They are meromorphic, including at branch points and at infinity, with only finite-order poles. By the Liouville-type argument (Riemann's §§ on functions on the simple plane) they are rational functions r_k(z). Hence w^n - r_1 w^(n-1) + ... + (-1)^n r_n = 0. In the simply covered case w itself is rational.

(3) A crossed-out passage was replaced by the right-column text. Riemann declines to develop the theory of 'einfache Abhängigkeitsgesetze'. He also declines to discuss the bridging question: whether his concept of a complex-differentiable function (defined via the Cauchy–Riemann condition) coincides with that of a dependence expressible by Größenoperationen.

(4) §21. An executed example is to illustrate the general theorems. The application in §20 (algebraic and Abelian-type functions) is the intended one but very special. The argument runs as follows:
- If the dependence is given by finitely many operations, the function has finitely many parameters.
- So a sufficient system of independent boundary and discontinuity conditions cannot contain conditions freely prescribable at every point of a line, that is, an arbitrary function along a curve.
- Therefore an example in which the function depends on an arbitrary function is preferable.

A draft phrase about an 'astronomical' example is deleted. The chosen example is put in the geometric dress of the end of §18: relating two given surfaces to each other so that point corresponds to point and boundary to boundary. This is the conformal mapping problem, which leads to the Riemann mapping theorem in §21 of the published text.
errors: No computational errors. The algebraicity statement is correct provided the covering of the plane is finitely-sheeted ('mehrfach' must mean finitely many times). The poles must be finitely many, which follows from compactness plus isolatedness.

The §21 heuristic is a plausibility argument, not a proof: 'finitely many operations implies finitely many parameters implies no conditions arbitrary along a line'. Both 'parameter' and 'Größenoperation' are left informal, and the parameters may be arbitrary constants.

The deferred question (does every function in Riemann's sense coincide with one expressible by finitely many operations?) is, read literally, false in general. Riemann leaves it explicitly 'unerörtert'.

results.what: A function on a finitely-sheeted covering of the full extended plane whose only singularities are finite-order poles is an algebraic function of z.
results.modern_name: Meromorphic functions on a compact Riemann surface are algebraic (the function field of a compact Riemann surface is an algebraic function field)

results.what: Programmatic principle: classes of functions are characterised by boundary and discontinuity conditions rather than by analytic expressions.
Announcement of the conformal mapping example: relate two given surfaces pointwise, boundary to boundary.
results.modern_name: Riemann mapping theorem / conformal mapping problem (Dissertation §21)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 (rigorous proofs by Osgood 1900, Koebe, Carathéodory)

results.what: Draft remark that an 'astronomical' example (a function given by finitely many operations) was considered and rejected in favour of one depending on an arbitrary function.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of text that appears almost verbatim in the published 1851 dissertation (§20 and the opening of §21). The algebraicity theorem and the conformal-mapping program are famously Riemann's. The only new detail is the deleted mention of an 'astronomical' example, which is a minor drafting curiosity.

checkable.asserts: The symmetric functions over the two sheets of sqrt(z)+1/(z-1) are rational. The product equals w**2 - 2*w/(z-1) + 1/(z-1)**2 - z, so w satisfies a polynomial with rational coefficients.
This expression equals 0, confirming that the algebraic equation is satisfied by the 2-sheeted meromorphic function.
Equals 1. In the local parameter t=1/z at infinity, z = 1/t is a first-order infinity, matching Riemann's convention that z itself counts as an infinity of first order at z = infinity.

transcription_corrections: Right column, top: 'zu den entsprechenden Ausdrücken, wozu die Function fortsetzt übergehen' should almost certainly read 'zu den verschiedenen Ausdrücken, deren die Function fähig ist, übergehen'. Compare the deleted draft on the previous page: 'zu den verschiedenen Ausdrücken, deren sie fähig ist, überzugehen'.
Line 1: 'Der Character und Gattung' is probably 'Der Character einer Gattung von Functionen'.
Line 2: the doubled 'bestimmte' is a transcription artifact. The word inserted above the line is likely 'ähnliche' ('auf ähnliche Art'), with 'bestimmte' as the original or a variant.
Last line: 'jedem Bezeichnungspunkte' is more likely 'jedem Begrenzungspunkte'. This is consistent with the margin 'Begr' and the next page's 'Begrenzungs... entspricht'.
Right column, lower: 'nicht ein derlei[?] astronomisches Beispiel' plausibly reads 'nicht ein derartiges astronomisches Beispiel'.
